previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 60-year-old man was admitted for evaluation of atypical chest pain and worsening shortness of breath. Initial concern for cardiac ischemia was ruled out with serial troponins and a normal stress MIBI test showing no perfusion defects and preserved ejection fraction. His chest pain was determined to be non-cardiac, possibly musculoskeletal. Shortness of breath was attributed to COPD, with oxygen desaturation on exertion, leading to initiation of inhaled bronchodilators and home oxygen therapy. Hypothyroidism was identified with elevated TSH and low free T4, prompting an increase in levothyroxine dose. The patient was monitored for alcohol withdrawal without complications and engaged in plans for outpatient support. He was discharged stable with new prescriptions, follow-up arranged with pulmonology and primary care, and instructions for medication adherence and symptom monitoring.

radiology_notes.text:
INDICATION:  ___ man with dizziness.

___.

TECHNIQUE:  Non-contrast head CT.

FINDINGS:  There is no evidence of hemorrhage, edema, mass effect, change in
ventricular size, or infarction.  Again noted and stable in appearance is
extensive periventricular and subcortical white matter hypodensity consistent
with a chronic small vessel change, a lacune in the left basal ganglia, an
area of prior infarct in the right parietal region, and moderate involutional
change.  Bilateral cavernous carotid artery calcifications are stable.  The
paranasal sinuses and mastoid air cells are clear.  There is likely cerumen in
both external auditory canals.  The patient is edentulous.

IMPRESSION:  No evidence of hemorrhage or mass effect.  Chronic changes as
above.  For the detection of acute brain ischemia, MRI with diffusion is more
sensitive than non-contrast head CT.
